selectionPolicy: A declared initial set spanning the compatibility reference, direct Chrome automation, an integrated browser test runner and the WebDriver/BiDi ecosystem. Inclusion does not assert a popularity rank or an unmeasured speed ranking. Expand the set when a relevant faster contender is identified.

competitors.reason: Compatibility reference and established end-to-end runner; existing matched library-flow baseline.
Direct Chrome automation contender with native locator readiness and low-level browser control; useful for testing whether the independent engine beats an automation library as well as a runner.
Integrated end-to-end runner with browser-side command execution and retrying assertions; its event model and runner costs require a separate suite comparison.
WebDriver/BiDi ecosystem contender with native user interactions and standalone or runner execution; record the actual negotiated protocol and browser driver.
User-requested runtime-integrated browser automation contender. Start with its Chrome backend for a matched-browser comparison; system WebKit requires a separate cross-browser class.
competitors.admissionRequirements: The native Chrome draft completes seven fixture outcomes, but per-view storage is shared and input/readiness, failure diagnostics, launch policy and cleanup differ. All equivalence, resource and performance admission flags remain false. The historical broad-matrix coordinator does not implement this adapter.

lifecycleFollowup.scope: Raw Browser.close works in selected Linux controls; descendant adoption remains and nine of twelve captures require collector termination. Native adapter unchanged; no resource/performance admission.

samplingObservation.scope: Seven native categories sampled with original wrapper exit and descendant drain; shared storage, native flags/actions, timeout failure and force-kill shutdown remain distinct from reference semantics. No cross-engine ranking or resource admission.

admission.policy: Functional admission runs retain observations and elapsed time but do not enter performance tables as comparative measurements. Successful application outcomes, exact request counts, trusted events, fresh-context isolation, launch identity and clean watchdog exit are mandatory. Deviations from the reference operation/event contract must be reported explicitly.

performancePolicy: Use the independent-launch sampling, exclusion, uncertainty and regression thresholds in baseline.json. Library-flow observations do not stand in for full runner-suite or contention results. No current broad competitor leadership claim.
